origins.section: One Binary per Project and Start Year Turns "When" Into "Whether"
A Project Starts at Most Once, and a Must-Do Starts Exactly Once
A Timing Window Is Enforced by the Variables You Never Create

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-why-binaries: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.pass:q-why-binaries: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-why-binaries: "Why not one integer variable 'start year' per project ...? Because every quantity that depends on the start year (the NPV, the spend in each year, the crews needed) would then be a nonlinear function of that integer. With one binary per year, each of them is a plain sum ... linear in the x."
recorded.prompt:q-once: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.pass:q-once: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-once: "Nothing so far stops the model from starting a project in 2027 and in 2029, and collecting its NPV twice. One constraint per project closes that: sum_t x_{i,t} <= 1"; "Forget the 'at most once' row ... with a project listed twice."
recorded.prompt:q-window: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.pass:q-window: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-window: "A project with a three-year cost profile that starts in 2030 would still be spending in 2032, outside the plan ... check that t + duration - 1 is inside the horizon for every variable you create" (2033+3-1=2035 > 2034).

recorded.prompt:q-why-binaries:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-why-binaries:a: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-why-binaries:a: The page names the cost as nonlinearity ("would then be a nonlinear function of that integer"), not a fraction needing more constraints; the binary formulation is the one with more variables ("more variables, every expression linear").
recorded.prompt:q-why-binaries:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-why-binaries:c: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-why-binaries:c: The page names a real cost: every start-year-dependent quantity "would then be a nonlinear function of that integer".
recorded.prompt:q-why-binaries:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-why-binaries:d: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-why-binaries:d: NPV is listed among the quantities that "would then be a nonlinear function of that integer"; it is a plain sum only "With one binary per year".
recorded.prompt:q-once:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-once:a: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-once:a: An at-least-once row does not stop a second start; the missing row is sum <= 1 ("Forget the 'at most once' row and the failure is quiet ... a project listed twice").
recorded.prompt:q-once:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-once:b: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-once:b: The page attributes a twice-listed project to a missing "at most once" row, not a budget row.
recorded.prompt:q-once:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-once:d: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-once:d: "A Timing Window Is Enforced by the Variables You Never Create" - there is no window row; and a double start is the at-most-once row's job.
recorded.prompt:q-window:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-window:b: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-window:b: Same passage: a 2033 start ends in 2035, outside the horizon, so "the model will fund work it never pays for".
recorded.prompt:q-window:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-window:c: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-window:c: "P001 may start in 2028 or 2029, so x[P001,2027] does not exist"; the window is enforced by not creating variables, not by the solver discarding years.
recorded.prompt:q-window:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.pass:q-window:d: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-window:d: Variables only for years in the window ("create x_{i,t} only for e_i <= t <= l_i"), and the horizon check rules out late starts.
